correctness.rationale: Incidence graph of any finite thick generalized quadrangle (s,t) has girth eight, diameter four, |P|=(s+1)(st+1), |L|=(t+1)(st+1), |E|=(s+1)(t+1)(st+1), hence first Betti b=(st)^2. At scale one its Rips is G. At scale two the high-girth simplicial collapse onto G is valid. At scale three all point-to-line edges exist and the two induced same-type clique complexes each homotopy-retract onto incidence G, giving their join ≃∨^{b²} S³. At scale four the diameter makes a full simplex. The inclusion at scales one to two is a collapse, fixing H1 persistence, so bars b times [1,3) in H1 and b² times [3,4) in H3, no other positive-degree bars.

originality.rationale: The exact scale-three join and b²-sphere formula for EVERY finite thick generalized quadrangle already appears in the published full finding Scale-three Vietoris–Rips complexes of finite generalized quadrangles. Independently, Adamaszek Proposition 2.2 proves simplicial collapse from graph square to the original graph whenever girth≥7, covering all generalized-quadrangle incidence graphs (girth 8). Diameter-four termination and Euler rank are immediate. Their combination implies the entire proposed two-stage persistence formula.
residual_risks: The published high-girth collapse and scale-three join may have distinct historical publication dates; originality judgment concerns implication and present mathematical coverage.
The zero-dimensional barcode was not asserted, and no conclusion for other generalized polygons or weighted metrics is warranted.
